note: Demo findings for the AI Security Co-pilot. Shape matches lib/passive-recon/types.ts Finding[]. On build day, plan A replaces this with buildFindings() over a live BulletRecon scan; the deterministic demo set stays as the offline fallback so the 90-second demo can never break on a dead network.

findings.title: AWS Access Key in client-side JavaScript
findings.detail: Pattern matched in a bundle served to every visitor. Confirm whether the value is live before reporting.

findings.title: Possible subdomain takeover: blog.acme-startup.example
findings.detail: The CNAME points at a known service that no longer claims this host, so an attacker could register it and serve content on your domain.

findings.title: SPF allows any sender (+all)
findings.detail: The policy explicitly authorises every host on the internet to send as this domain.

findings.title: Missing Strict-Transport-Security
findings.detail: Without HSTS, a returning visitor can be downgraded to plain HTTP by a network attacker before the redirect to HTTPS happens.

findings.title: Session-like cookie "sessionid" is missing flags
findings.detail: Set-Cookie for sessionid has no HttpOnly, no SameSite.
findings.evidence: sessionid served from 10.0.14.22 behind the load balancer

findings.title: DMARC policy is p=none
findings.detail: The domain monitors spoofing but instructs receivers to deliver it anyway.

findings.title: 2 source maps referenced
findings.detail: Source maps usually reconstruct original, unminified source — including comments, internal paths and dead code.

findings.title: robots.txt names 3 sensitive-looking paths
findings.detail: Disallow entries are a curated list of what the operator would rather nobody visited — start there.

findings.title: No CAA record
findings.detail: Any public CA may issue a certificate for this domain; CAA restricts that to named issuers.

findings.title: DNSSEC is not enabled
findings.detail: Responses for this zone are not signed, so cache-poisoning defences rely on transport alone.
